subject: POC criteria and next actions — CobaltAI discovery follow-up
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@cobaltai.com>, Tom Rogers <tom.rogers@cobaltai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 04 May 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: POC criteria and next actions — CobaltAI discovery follow-up

Hi Alyssa / Tom —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a proposed trial (POC) plan so we can get alignment before Ben and Kim start sizing infra and test harnesses. High-level ask: confirm these success criteria and owners so we can lock a 6-week trial window.

Summary of needs you mentioned:
- Inference for document summarization and structured extraction pipelines (avg doc length ~1.2k tokens)
- Latency requirement: 95th percentile < 450ms for single-request infer calls under production-like load
- Throughput: baseline 30 rps sustained during spike windows (burst to 80 rps)
- Cost target: target effective cost <= $0.004/token for production-like mix (batching and quantization considered)
- Accuracy/quality: ROUGE-L >= 0.66 on your internal test set; low hallucination on named-entity extraction

Proposed POC success matrix (attached spreadsheet: COB_trial_success_matrix.xlsx) — please review, but the core gates are:
1) Latency gate: 95p < 450ms on synthetic load that mimics your 95th pct size distribution.
2) Throughput gate: sustained 30 rps for 30 minutes without error rate > 1%.
3) Token economics: measured cost/token during the trial (post-batching) <= $0.004 target (we'll show breakdown of batch sizes, cache hit rates, and quantization steps).
4) Quality gate: evaluation on your labeled set: ROUGE-L and entity precision thresholds as listed in the sheet.

Ownership (proposed):
- Redwood: Ben (ops/benchmarks) and Kim (security/compliance integration)
- CobaltAI: Alyssa (product/quality owner) and Tom (infra lead)

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm the success matrix and owners by EOD Wednesday (5/6).
- Ben will schedule a 1-hour kick-off to capture sample payloads and network egress/peering needs (aim for next week).
- Kim will request your security questionnaire & IP/data flow diagram; Ben will stand up an initial sandbox image for benchmarking after we get sample data.

If that looks good I’ll open the trial and share a short runbook.

Thanks —
Dylan

--
Dylan Brooks

Subject: Re: POC criteria and next actions — CobaltAI discovery follow-up

Dylan —

Thanks for the clear recap. Couple of quick questions from our infra team before we confirm owners/date:
1) Is the 95p latency target measured cold-start excluded (we expect some model warm-up) and using your recommended batch size?
2) For the throughput gate, do you expect continuous open connections / streaming or synchronous REST calls?
3) On cost/token: our mix includes higher-length documents (2k+ tokens) ~15% of traffic — will the token cost target be measured on mixed distribution or median doc size?

Alyssa, can you confirm that legal will want the trial IP/data terms (we will share a standard DPA + trial SOW)? I’ve looped legal at legal@cobaltai.com.

Tom
Principal Infra Engineer, CobaltAI
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Tom Rogers <tom.rogers@cobaltai.com>, Alyssa Chen <alyssa@cobaltai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 04 May 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC criteria and next actions — CobaltAI discovery follow-up

Tom — great questions, thanks. Quick clarifications so we measure the same thing:

1) Latency: we will exclude cold-starts for the 95p gate. Our benchmark harness will perform a 10-minute warm-up and use steady-state requests after that. We'll surface both cold-start and steady-state distribution in the report.
2) Throughput: trial uses synchronous REST calls (your normal production client path). We’ll also run a separate streaming profile if you want to explore that later.
3) Cost/token: we will report cost across your mixed distribution (weighted by the sample traffic you provide). The POC gate will be evaluated on the mixed distribution; the spreadsheet has a column that models the 85/15 split for doc sizes so you can see sensitivity.

If that aligns I’ll mark owners and have Ben kick off the benchmark plan. We’ll also include a short baseline run showing our default quantized variant vs. a 16-bit baseline so you can see the trade-offs.

Action items:
- Alyssa: confirm owners and legal contact by EOD Wed 5/6.
- Tom: send a small sample payload set (50–100 docs) and your traffic distribution CSV to ben.carter@redwood.com.
- Ben: draft an initial benchmark schedule and invite a 60-min kick-off for next Wed/Thu.

Thanks —
Dylan
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@cobaltai.com>, Tom Rogers <tom.rogers@cobaltai.com>

Subject: Re: POC criteria and next actions — CobaltAI discovery follow-up

Hi all —

I pulled together an initial trial runbook and the success matrix into COB_trial_success_matrix.xlsx (attached). A few practical notes up front:
- Network: if you want predictable 95p latency we recommend either a direct VPC peering or a dedicated egress path. Attached network_requirements.pdf lists minimum bandwidth and port/rules we use for dedicated trials.
- Measurement: I’ll run three 30-minute steady-state runs after warm-up for each configuration (quantized variant, fp16 baseline) and aggregate 95/99p latencies and error rates.
- Instrumentation: please include a header x-cobalt-request-id in the sample payloads so we can map requests back to your logs during the trial.

Proposed kickoff times (PT): Wed 05/12 10:00 or Thu 05/13 14:00 — I’ll set the calendar once you pick one.

Deliverables by end of POC (6 weeks):
- Full performance report (latency/throughput/cost breakdown by batch size and model variant)
- Quality evaluation on your labeled set with examples of failure cases
- Runbook for prod conversion including rollout and canary steps

If you confirm the time I’ll also share an Azure/GCP networking checklist and a short SOW to make sure legal has what it needs.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: COB_trial_success_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet summary), network_requirements.pdf (1 page)
